one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings are not yet confirmed by Uber IR; calendars point to Nov 3 pre-market (last year's Q3 was Nov 4 pre-market) [9,29], so most likely inside the window ending Nov 4. Guide: GB $58.25-60.25B (+18-22% cc), adj. EBITDA $2.86-2.96B, non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 [1]. Uber usually meets or beats its own guide, but the stock has often sold off on prints when the next-quarter guide or AV-spend commentary disappoints, so the earnings reaction is roughly symmetric. Mild support: the CEO ($10.0M at $70.96, 2026-09-10) and COO ($5.3M at ~$75.8) bought in the open market (Form 4s [28]), so management sees value near today's price. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends Nov 5 [2], just after the window. I no longer use the AltIndex September download spike: I could not find a second source for it, and the supervisor discounted it. Robotaxi headlines are a slow negative drift, but verified Tesla driverless scale is still tiny (~85-300 unsupervised cars in 6 cities [26,13]). Net: no directional edge. I center at ~$69.9 with lognormal sigma 11% (monthly vol 35%/3.5 = 10%, widened slightly for the earnings event).

EBITDA $15.8B, haircut 7% to $14.7B, x 9.5x NTM peer median = $140B EV; ~zero net debt ex-Delivery Hero; 2.0B shares = $70). Delivery Hero assumed value-neutral at the price paid.

On a consistent NTM consensus basis the 10-peer median is 19.6x (core-7 18.0x; range 12.8x EXPE to 47.7x DASH) [25,7], up from the 18.2x mixed-basis median I used in round 1. UBER trades at 16.6x NTM today [25]. I keep a ~15% discount to the all-peer median (~8% below core): Uber's EPS growth is above the median, but the AV overhang is verified and persists through the horizon. Waymo's own app launches in Austin/Atlanta in Jan 2028 and Uber said the change lets it add other AV providers [24], so the terminal-value question that caps the multiple will not be resolved by Oct-2027. Dolphin's ~15-16x 2027 earnings [21] is a cross-check. 16.5x (vs 16x in round 1) reflects the higher reconciled median and the verified insider buying [28], but no re-rating beyond today's multiple. bear.story: Robotaxi disintermediation becomes consensus: Waymo reaches ~1M weekly rides and steers demand to its own app ahead of the Jan-2028 Austin/Atlanta launch, Tesla scales driverless beyond its current ~100-300 cars, mobility take rate and AV economics disappoint, and Delivery Hero leverage plus AV capex weigh. Multiple compresses to ~11x on ~$4.5 EPS, or ~6.5x EBITDA like Lyft.

base.story: Bookings grow high-teens, EBITDA +20%, FCF >$12B funds buybacks; AV remains <1% of trips and is additive through Uber's network. No re-rating: Uber stays near today's ~16.5x NTM P/E (and ~9.5-10x EBITDA, about the peer median), so the return is EPS compounding plus buybacks.

bull.story: The aggregator thesis proves out: AV partners launch through Uber in many cities, vehicle financing moves off balance sheet, DH integration adds scale, and the P/E re-rates to the ~19-20x peer median on ~$5.2 EPS.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. On P/E, a modest discount despite above-median growth because the AV disintermediation risk specific to Uber and Lyft is verified and persists past the horizon (Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta from Jan 2028; contract through at least May 2028 [24]). On EV/EBITDA I use the median: Uber's faster EBITDA growth is offset by adjusted EBITDA excluding SBC and future AV fleet costs. Lyft's ~6.4x NTM EV/EBITDA (vs ~18x GAAP NTM P/E) is the cleaner read of how the market prices AV risk, so it anchors the bear case rather than the P/E. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Sourcing note: the 19.6x / 18.0x P/E and 9.4x / 8.5x EV/EBITDA medians (and UBER 16.6x / 11.1x) came from aggregator multiples (round-1 MarketScreener GAAP-mixed P/E; stockanalysis EV). Rebuilt from each company's Q2 2026 release (EV) and S&P Global adjusted NTM consensus EPS, the all-peer medians are 16.6x P/E (core-7 13.3x) and 9.2x EV/EBITDA (core-7 7.9x); UBER is 16.7x and 11.3x. The per-peer values in this file are left as the agent's round-2 read; supervisor.json comps_review carries the verified table.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$53 (about 10.8x my haircut NTM EPS, ~7.2x NTM EBITDA, near Lyft's AV-discounted ~6.4x, and ~19% under the 52-week low of $65.41) the market would be pricing structural impairment, not volatility: e.g. Waymo or Tesla pulling supply off Uber before the 2028 dates, mobility take-rate erosion, bookings growth below ~12%, or a Delivery Hero financing problem. It would also be ~25% below where the CEO and COO bought in September, so management's own value view would be clearly wrong.

reasoning: Round 2. Fundamentals are verified and strong: Q2-26 GB $58.0B (+22% cc), adj. EBITDA $2.8B (+33%), TTM FCF >$10B, Q3 guide EPS +28-35% [1]. The supervisor's main correction applies to me: my '~17x' peer EV/EBITDA median was extrapolated from trailing GAAP data. On a consistent NTM basis the median is 9.4x and UBER is at 11.1x, so EBITDA comps support no re-rating [25,7]. Re-running that leg at the 9.5x median gives $70 (was $81). The reconciled NTM P/E median is higher (19.6x, core 18x), so I lift my P/E to 16.5x (about today's multiple), giving $81. I weight P/E 55% because the EBITDA peer set is dominated by slow-growth OTAs and adjusted EBITDA flatters on SBC. Blended fair value is $76, down from $80. I differ from the supervisor's $79 because I do not put a 17.5x P/E on the stock while the post-2028 AV question is open. New facts: CEO/COO open-market buys of ~$15M at $71-76 in September (Form 4s [28]) are a modest positive. Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta from Jan 2028 runs alongside Uber with cars on Uber through at least May 2028 [24], so it is a multiple cap, not a 12-month volume hit; I already treated it that way. My lane's evidence still says the near-term AV threat is small: Waymo ~500k paid rides/week on ~3,500-4,000 cars [27,8] vs ~300M Uber trips/week [1]; Tesla's verified driverless fleet is ~85-300 cars in 6 cities (two independent trackers [26,13]); Waymo fares ran above Uber's [14]. Discounted per the supervisor: the AltIndex download spike [15] (no second source found; removed from the argument) and the 2024 X post [23]. Scenarios are $49/$75/$99 at 25/50/25%. The ladder is a three-component lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.20) with a median of ~$74.4 and P(>=70) = 0.58, down from 0.605. Upside is EPS compounding plus buybacks, held back by negative momentum. The spread is ~35-40%, in line with realized vol. Lane note: excluding the basic company filings, about 62% of sources are alternative/newsletter/prediction-market; NTM comps rely on MarketScreener tables, which Uber's own page shows with a stale Feb-2026 reference price, so the multiples are recomputed at current prices.
